name: uri-hex-ipv4-host-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees uniformResourceIdentifier is 'example.com'. The leaf's URI SAN is 'foo://0xde.0xad.0xbe.0xef/path' — a host whose labels are all hex literals that getaddrinfo / inet_pton would parse as an IPv4 address (222.173.190.239). RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 prohibits an IP-literal in a URI subjected to URI name constraints (the URI name-constraint matches hostnames, with iPAddress being a separate GeneralName type). A validator that treats the value as a DNS hostname would scan the trailing label '0xef' against the constraint and reject for length; one that resolves it as IPv4 should reject it as IP-shaped.
references: BoringSSL b84dc606 — crypto/x509: Tighten URI name constraints parsing and matching
notes: Complements uri-ip-host-invalid (dotted-decimal IPv4). The hex-prefixed form exists specifically because some parsers accept hex notations for IPv4 components, creating ambiguity between DNS hostname and IP-literal. BoringSSL post-b84dc606 rejects any URI host that parses to an IP-literal regardless of textual form, including 0x-prefixed labels.
